tools_helpful.evidence: Bulk Windows.UI.Xaml->Microsoft.UI.Xaml rewrite + MIGRATION-MAPPING.md triage table let the agent migrate all 7 scenarios; final build succeeded (session-log line 11754 'Build succeeded').
Its build gate surfaced the CS0104 batch as a hard FAIL so the agent had to fix them before declaring done (session-log line 9953 'Build failed with 17 error(s)').

tool_limitations.limitation: On a build FAIL it prints distinct CS#### codes but only a generic 'PATTERNS.md > Common build errors' pointer; it does not recognise the very common Windows.Web.Http/System.Net.Http CS0104 ambiguity and give the concrete fix.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add a targeted CS0104-Http detector that prints the disable-ImplicitUsings / alias fix.

failed_apis.why_tried: AdaptiveStreaming intercepts download requests via an IHttpFilter logger and AddAuthorizationHeaderFilter.
failed_apis.root_cause: IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync is typed with Windows.Web.Http.HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage; because System.Net.Http was also in scope (see CS0104), the compiler bound the override signature to the wrong types and reported CS0535 'does not implement interface member'.
failed_apis.fix: Remove System.Net.Http from scope (disable ImplicitUsings) so the Windows.Web.Http types bind, then the IHttpFilter implementation compiles.

special_apis.special_handling: UWP networking and AdaptiveMediaSource request-interception code uses the Windows.Web.Http stack, NOT System.Net.Http. These names collide 1:1 with System.Net.Http, so both namespaces cannot be in scope at once.

errors_encountered.error: CS0104: 'HttpClient'/'HttpRequestMessage'/'HttpResponseMessage' is an ambiguous reference between 'System.Net.Http.*' and 'Windows.Web.Http.*' (14 occurrences across ContentSelector, AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger, Scenario2-7)
errors_encountered.root_cause: The scaffold .csproj ships <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>, which injects a global 'using System.Net.Http'. The migrated source keeps its UWP 'using Windows.Web.Http;', so every Http* type name is ambiguous.
errors_encountered.fix: Set <ImplicitUsings>disable</ImplicitUsings> in the .csproj (session-log line 9960). Alternatives: <Using Remove="System.Net.Http" /> or per-file 'using HttpClient = Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient;'.

errors_encountered.error: CS0535: 'AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger'/'AddAuthorizationHeaderFilter' does not implement interface member 'IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync(HttpRequestMessage)'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Cascade of the CS0104 ambiguity — the override resolved HttpRequestMessage to System.Net.Http instead of Windows.Web.Http, so it no longer matched the interface.
errors_encountered.fix: Same fix as CS0104 (remove System.Net.Http from scope).

errors_encountered.error: XamlCompiler WMC1509 / 'Xaml Internal Error WMC9999: Object reference not set to an instance of an object' during MarkupCompilePass2
errors_encountered.root_cause: Cascade of the failed C# compile — MarkupCompilePass2 could not load the LocalAssembly because the project failed to build on the CS0104 errors. Disappeared once the C# errors were fixed.
errors_encountered.fix: Fix the underlying CS0104 compile errors; the markup-compiler crash was downstream, not independent.

errors_encountered.error: MSB 'The process cannot access the file ... AdaptiveStreaming.dll ... because it is being used by another process' (interop.targets 724) — Build failed with 1 error
errors_encountered.root_cause: A previously launched instance of the app was still running while the agent rebuilt, locking the output dll.
errors_encountered.fix: Stop the running app process before rebuilding; transient/environmental, not a code defect.

dev_agent_struggles.where: First full build after migration (session-log lines 9900-9960)
dev_agent_struggles.symptom: 17 build errors, 14 of them the same CS0104 Http ambiguity across 8 files, plus 2 CS0535 and a cascading WMC9999 XAML markup-compiler crash.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: Resolved in one diagnosis: edited the .csproj ImplicitUsings from enable to disable, which cleared all 14 CS0104 + 2 CS0535 + the WMC9999 cascade at once.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Scaffold .csproj default <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings> injects global System.Net.Http, colliding with the UWP Windows.Web.Http stack the sample uses.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Documenting the Windows.Web.Http vs System.Net.Http CS0104 ambiguity (and the ImplicitUsings root cause + fix) in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, and having Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 emit a targeted hint when it sees CS0104 on Http types.

env_issues.issue: Output dll locked by a still-running app instance during rebuild (interop.targets 724).
env_issues.workaround: Stop the running AdaptiveStreaming process before rebuilding.
